papers.title_en: LayerCanvas: Infographic Generation in AI Learning Assistants via Hybrid Layer-Set Diffusion
papers.authors: Keshav Gupta, Jeremy Owen, Christopher Lloyd, Shaunak Mishra, Manav Sharma
papers.evidence: AI学习助手生成个性化信息图辅助辅导
papers.tldr: 在线学习助手需要自动生成兼具视觉表现、准确排版和可编辑性的信息图，但SVG美观性有限，栅格扩散又会压平结构与文本。LayerCanvas以SVG保留语义结构、文本和可编辑性，将元素按z序划分为互不重叠集合，并通过并行RGB扩散流进行美化。它显著提升文本保真度，并取得最高整体美学质量，还支持无损编辑、本地化、资产复用与动画。
papers.abstract_en: Online learning platforms are increasingly deploying AI assistants to provide personalized, on-demand tutoring. These can leverage infographics to communicate complex information and improve the learning experience. However, automating effective infographic generation remains a challenging task, requiring a combination of visual richness with precise typography, structured layouts, and continued editability. Existing representation methods satisfy these goals only in part: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) representations preserve geometry, hierarchy, and text but provide limited aesthetic flexibility, while raster diffusion models produce richer appearances by flattening content and layout into a single image. Conditioning a diffusion model on a rasterized SVG does not resolve this conflict because the raster preserves approximate placement but discards element ownership, occlusion relationships, and the structure needed to modify and recompose the result. We introduce LayerCanvas, a hybrid approach that retains SVG as the semantic, structural, and typographic program while using diffusion to aestheticize non-text content. Rather than generating one flattened raster, LayerCanvas partitions SVG elements into z-ordered sets of mutually non-overlapping elements and processes them through communicating parallel RGB generation streams. The resulting layers are independently editable and deterministically recomposed, while text is rendered from preserved vector metadata. Our approach combines rich visual synthesis with accurate typography and localized editing. LayerCanvas substantially improves text fidelity over state-of-the-art raster image generators while achieving the highest overall aesthetic quality. We further demonstrate non-destructive content editing, localization, asset reuse, and animation.

papers.title_en: A Framework for Teaching the Responsible and Effective Use of Generative AI in Statistics and Data Science
papers.authors: Vinny Davies, Craig Alexander, Jennifer Gaskell, Matthew Parker, Jake Lever
papers.evidence: 在数据科学教育中教授生成式AI负责任使用的框架
papers.tldr: 生成式AI进入统计与数据科学教学后，学生使用对话式工具的机会增加，但可靠性、透明性、隐私与学术规范问题突出。论文提出一个教学框架，围绕理解、开发、报告与安全四个领域组织课程内容。该框架已在MOOC、短期培训和本硕课程中实施，并结合反馈迭代。作者总结真实分析任务、批判评估输出、整合负责任实践与保持灵活性等设计要点。
papers.abstract_en: The rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence (AI) following the public release of tools such as ChatGPT has begun to reshape how students engage with coding, statistical analysis, and written communication in higher education. Growing use of conversational AI systems creates opportunities for learning alongside challenges around reliability, transparency, privacy, and appropriate academic and professional practice, highlighting the need for structured education in their responsible use. This paper presents a framework for teaching the responsible and effective use of generative AI in statistics and data science. The framework is organised around four areas: Understanding, Development, Reporting, and Safety, covering conceptual foundations, practical interaction within analytical workflows, documentation and transparency, and issues including reliability, bias, privacy, and ethics. Its design draws on emerging work in AI literacy and established principles from statistics and data science education, and was further refined through workshop and conference activities and participant feedback. The framework has been implemented across multiple settings, including a massive open online course, short training sessions, and undergraduate and postgraduate skills-based teaching. We use these experiences to identify broader design considerations for educators, including the value of authentic analytical tasks, critical evaluation of generated outputs, integrated consideration of responsible practice, and flexibility as generative AI technologies continue to evolve.

papers.title_en: Multi-sourced AI Tutor for Non-Native English Speaker Students
papers.authors: Yiyin Shen, Xinyi Ai, Weibing Wang, Rogers Jeffrey Leo John, Meenakshi Syamkumar
papers.evidence: 面向计算机教育的AI导师与双语学习支持
papers.tldr: 非英语母语学生在计算机课程中常因语言障碍而难以获得及时、有效的答疑支持。为此，作者开发通用AI导师系统，支持以中文等外语提问，并利用带新型问题抽取机制的多源RAG流程检索课程材料，生成双语回答与技术术语表。基于91条Piazza帖子评测，系统对83.52%的问题给出正确且有帮助的回答，76.92%的翻译质量较高，64.47%可生成术语表。研究说明多源RAG可增强AI导师对非母语学生的支持，弥补传统助教资源的不足。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non-native English speaker (NNES) students face in computing courses due to language barriers. To aid such students, we developed a general-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages (currently focused on Mandarin) and provide bilingual responses. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner. The tutor also provided high-quality translations for 76.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64.47% of them. Our findings underscore the potential of multi-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course.

papers.title_en: EduWild: How Teacher-Configured Chatbots Fail in Real-World Use and How to Fix Them
papers.authors: Ziqi Liu, Ruiwei Xiao, Yuxuan Li, John Stamper
papers.evidence: 教师配置的教育聊天机器人及其真实教学失败模式
papers.tldr: 教师正通过自然语言配置教育聊天机器人，但这些机器人在真实课堂中的失败模式仍缺乏系统认识。EduWild汇集1726段对话、217个教师配置机器人及其指令配置，其中含35个部署机器人的900段真实用户对话，并建立29类失败分类体系。分析显示，机器人常跳过必需流程步骤、缺少期望设定，并以信息或问题让学习者过载。基于高频失败模式设计的提示框架，在200名大学生、10个机器人研究中将每段对话目标失败码均值从1.406降至0.489。
papers.abstract_en: Teachers increasingly configure educational chatbots through natural-language instructions, but how these bots fail in real-world use remains poorly understood. We introduce EduWild, a dataset of 1,726 conversations with 217 teacher-configured chatbots, each paired with the instructions and configuration behind it, including 900 conversations from the intended end users of 35 deployed chatbots. We develop a 29-code taxonomy covering factual, workflow, diagnostic, and pedagogical failures and apply it using a human-calibrated LLM judge. The most frequent failures are lapses in following teacher intent --- bots skip required workflow steps (53.8% of end-user conversations), omit expectation setup (33.4%), and overload learners with information or questions (37.1%). Guided by these findings, we design a prompt-based harness targeting the six most frequent failure modes. In a study with 200 college students across ten bots, the harness reduces the mean number of target failure codes per conversation from 1.406 to 0.489, a 65.2% relative reduction with bots weighted equally. These findings show how real-world failure analysis can guide practical improvements to educational chatbots.

papers.title_en: MAVE: A Multi-Agent Framework for Grounded Pedagogical Feedback from Online Class Videos
papers.authors: Qingyue Chen, Huaiyuan Yao, Wanpeng Xu, Varun Shourie, Qianwen Wang, Hua Wei
papers.evidence: 基于在线课堂视频的多智能体教学反馈
papers.tldr: 在线课堂视频长且噪声大，学生响应难定位，自动反馈常泛泛而谈、缺乏课堂证据支撑。MAVE将教学反馈拆为课程梳理、多模态观察、行为评估与建议生成四个智能体角色，把教学目标与时间对齐的语音、视觉和互动证据连接起来。作者构建MAVEBench，含173个知识点片段、约20小时真实课堂视频。实验显示MAVE在诊断正确性、教学对齐性和可操作性上优于直接提示、Reflexion和TextGrad，为有据可依的教学反馈提供框架与基准。
papers.abstract_en: Timely pedagogical feedback is difficult to scale in online classes, where long and noisy videos make student responses hard to locate and automated systems often produce generic advice weakly grounded in actual classroom behavior. The key challenge is to connect the instructional goal of a specific lesson segment with temporally aligned multimodal evidence of student responses, and then translate the observed gap into an actionable teaching move. We introduce MAVE (Multi-Agents for Video-based Educational Feedback), a multi-agent framework for grounded pedagogical feedback from online-class videos. MAVE decomposes feedback generation into four roles: the Curator structures the lesson and infers expected student activity; the Observer extracts aligned speech, visual, and interaction evidence; the Assessor estimates the activity supported by student behavior; and the Advisor generates gap-conditioned teaching recommendations. To evaluate this capability, we introduce MAVEBench, a benchmark designed to measure whether feedback systems can ground diagnoses in multimodal student evidence, and generate actionable pedagogical feedback. MAVEBench contains 173 knowledge-point segments from approximately 20 hours of authentic online-class videos across STEM and Humanities, together with comprehensive simulation. Experiments show that MAVE outperforms direct prompting, Reflexion, and TextGrad in diagnostic correctness, instructional alignment, and actionability. Our code is available at https://github.com/DaRL-GenAI/MAVE

papers.title_en: Acharya 2.0: An AI Tutor for Self-Learning Subjects in Hindi
papers.authors: Shantipriya Parida, Debasish Dhal, Sonal Khosla, Sambit Sekhar, Muhammed Abdur Rahmaan Kamaldeen
papers.evidence: 面向印地语自学学科的AI导师
papers.tldr: 低资源语言缺乏标注数据和语言资源，印地语教育类智能辅导应用仍有限，RAG在英语外应用不足。本文提出RAG驱动的AI导师Acharya 2.0，以客户端-服务器Web应用为印地语学生提供课程内容检索与交互式学术辅助。摘要未报告量化评测，重点在系统设计与功能集成。其贡献是探索RAG在印地语教育场景的落地并促进教育公平。
papers.abstract_en: Text processing is crucial for low-resource languages as it enables the development of tools and technologies that bridge the digital divide and provide equitable access to information and services. By empowering low-resource languages with robust text processing, we can preserve linguistic diversity, enhance education, improve communi- cation, and foster inclusivity in a rapidly digitizing world. Due to the lack of sufficient annotated datasets and lin- guistic resources, it is challenging to develop accurate and reliable language technologies for these low-resource languages. Large Language Models (LLMs) have attracted sig- nificant attention with their performance and the value they produce. However, with the ever-evolving language, adapting LLMs for a specific task is time-consuming and resource-intensive. Thus, Retrieval-Augmented Genera- tion (RAG) has overcome this limitation by augmenting LLMs with external knowledge, thereby improving their efficiency and extensive task-specific adaptation. Most applications of the RAG technique have been limited to English and has seen limited application in In- dic languages. This paper introduces the RAG-powered AI-Tutor application, Acharya 2.0, designed to produce academic assistance to Hindi-speaking students. The client-server-based web application integrates many fea- tures to support students in accessing and interacting with educational content.

papers.title_en: AI Misconception and Adoption Among Indonesian K-12 Teachers
papers.authors: Alham Fikri Aji, Afifa Amriani, Rendi Chevi, Ayu Purwarianti, Derry Wijaya
papers.evidence: 调查中小学教师对AI的理解、使用与可接受性
papers.tldr: 印尼K-12教师AI应用受地理与基础设施不均制约，国家计划2025年推进AI进课堂，但教师准备度不明。研究通过半自动主题分析调查教师对AI的理解、师生使用方式及学习可接受性。结果显示教师普遍接受AI提效，却对学习深度与学术诚信风险保持警觉，且接受度高与对AI原理理解不足并存。研究揭示政策推进与教师认知之间的落差。
papers.abstract_en: Indonesia's fragmented geography and uneven infrastructure pose persistent challenges for adopting new educational technologies. While national initiatives aim to mainstream AI in K-12 schools by 2025, policy readiness does not automatically mean teachers are ready for the classroom. This study surveys Indonesian K-12 teachers to examine: (1) their understanding of AI, (2) how they and their students use AI, and (3) their views on the acceptability of AI in learning activities. Through semi-automated thematic analysis, we identify common misconceptions and use cases. Our findings reveal a notable mismatch: while teachers find AI use in education acceptable and support it for the sake of efficiency, they remain fully aware of the risks to learning depth and academic honesty. We also find that this high level of acceptance is currently coupled with a poor understanding of how AI actually works.

papers.title_en: Evaluating LLM-Generated Feedback on Handwritten Mathematics: Feedback Quality and Subsequent Exam Performance
papers.authors: Arne Vanhoyweghen, Vincent Holst, Melika Mobini, Lukas Van de Voorde, Tibo Vanleke, Andres Algaba, Sam Verboven, Marie-Anne Guerry, Filip Van Droogenbroeck, Vincent Ginis
papers.evidence: 大学数学中LLM生成的反馈与练习题
papers.tldr: 研究评估GPT-5.1从大学生手写数学答案与评分中生成反馈和练习题的质量，并检验反馈能否提升后续考试表现。作者在英语（n=343）与荷兰语（n=236）队列的六次周测中采用交叉反馈设计，并用六项标准由六名评审评估157条反馈。结果显示练习题获强评价比例最高（95.5%），诊断具体性（41.1%）与清晰度/语气（33.4%）较低，低分答案反馈可操作性更差。相关考题比较未发现校正后显著差异，但出勤与反馈暴露和更高成绩相关。
papers.abstract_en: We evaluate the quality of feedback and practice exercises generated by GPT-5.1 from handwritten university mathematics answers and their grades, and examine whether receiving this feedback improves subsequent exam performance. We use six weekly bonus tests in an English (n=343) and a Dutch (n=236) cohort. Tests 1 and 3 used a crossover feedback design; otherwise, all attendees received feedback. To evaluate the feedback, six reviewers assessed 157 messages from three English-cohort tasks using six criteria scored from 0 to 3. The practice exercises received the highest proportion of strong ratings (95.5%), while diagnostic specificity (41.1%) and clarity and tone (33.4%) received fewer. Feedback for the lowest-scoring answers was rated as less actionable, suggesting that these students may need more targeted guidance from instructors. Comparisons of related exam questions showed mixed results, with no statistically significant differences after adjustment across four comparisons. Greater attendance and feedback exposure were associated with higher exam scores, but the contribution of feedback could not be separated from attendance and practice. Our findings show the potential of an integrated framework merging instructor guidance with automated feedback generation to provide personalised learning support at scale.

papers.title_en: A Unified Response Framework for Questions and Tutoring Dialogues
papers.authors: Zhangqi Duan, Simon Woodhead, Maya Miller-Vedam, Andrew Lan
papers.evidence: 统一建模辅导对话与学生作答的IRT框架
papers.tldr: 现有学生建模多聚焦答题，难以利用师生辅导对话中的细粒度知识证据。本文提出统一框架，将问题回答与对话中导师提出的数学子任务映射到共享IRT量表，先识别并改写子任务为独立问题，再结合文本估计难度、追踪能力演化，并用导师动作正则化相邻子任务难度。在两个真实数学教育数据集上，该方法在题目难度预测与回答正确性预测上均优于强基线，为融合问答与辅导对话的学生建模提供了统一方案。
papers.abstract_en: Existing student models in educational applications largely focus on student responses to questions. However, as tutoring becomes more accessible at large scale, it is important to analyze dialogues between tutors and students, which may reveal fine-grained evidence on student knowledge. In this work, we propose a unified framework that models both student responses to questions and tutor-posed subtasks during dialogues on a shared item response theory (IRT) scale. We first identify mathematical subtasks in tutoring dialogues, rewrite them into self-contained questions, and identify the correctness of student responses to these subtasks. We then develop an IRT framework that estimates question/subtask difficulty from text, tracks students' evolving abilities across question-answering and dialogue interactions, and a novel method to leverages tutor moves between consecutive subtasks to regularize their difficulty values. We evaluate our framework on two real-world math education datasets containing both human- and AI-tutored dialogues. Results show that our framework outperforms strong baselines on both question difficulty prediction and response correctness prediction.

papers.title_en: HACHIMI-II: From Role-Play to Learner Behavior Modeling for Faithful Student Simulation
papers.authors: Yilin Jiang, Fei Tan, Xuanyu Yin, Jing Leng, Aimin Zhou
papers.evidence: 用于测试智能辅导系统与教学策略的模拟学生
papers.tldr: 让学生模拟器复现特定学习者的成败，是教学系统测试的前提，但常用的大模型角色扮演只演身份、不建模知识，导致模拟水平由模型自身能力决定、个体差异小且很少犯真实错误。HACHIMI-II 改为第三人称预测学习者下一步动作，用其历史构建学生模型、推断当前状态并编译为行为约束。三个题目作答数据集上模拟与真实能力分布距离缩小2.4–8.4倍，两个对话数据集上同类型、同位置、同机制的错误复现率提升1.8–5.1倍，消融显示增益主要来自显式学习者状态。
papers.abstract_en: Simulated students let researchers test tutoring systems and teaching strategies before real learners are available, but only if the simulation reproduces where a particular learner succeeds and fails. The common approach asks a large language model to role-play a student, but a role does not model what this learner knows or will do next, so the model's own competence fills the gap. Simulated students perform at a level set by the model, differ little from one another, and seldom make the real learners' errors. We model the learner's behavior and recast student simulation as third-person prediction of the learner's next action. HACHIMI-II builds a student model from the learner's history, infers the learner's state for the current item or tutor turn, and compiles it into a behavior harness that constrains the next action. On three item-response datasets, the Wasserstein-1 distance between simulated and real student ability is 2.4--8.4$\times$ smaller than that of the strongest baseline. On two dialogue datasets, HACHIMI-II reproduces real student errors with the same knowledge type, locus, and mechanism 1.8--5.1$\times$ more often than the strongest baseline, and ablations trace the gains mainly to the explicit learner state. Predicting the learner makes capable models usable as simulated students.

papers.title_en: MARS: A Momentum-Aware Adaptive Rating System for Personalized Assessment
papers.authors: Vikrant Sahu, Khethavath Sunil Naik, Gagan Raj Gupta
papers.evidence: 通过能力估计与题目推荐实现个性化学习的自适应测评系统
papers.tldr: 现有自适应评估常依赖固定难度、静态评分或黑盒预测，难以兼顾评分稳定、可解释与限时选题。MARS将题库建模为有向加权知识图谱，结合动态评分敏感度、响应质量与动量感知速度更新学习者熟练度，并在负分与时间预算下优化得分最大化选题。实验显示其评分更新比Fixed Elo更平滑，限时负分路由总分较最强基线高8.09，超时违规由50%降至5.6%。该工作为实时、可解释、易部署的自适应评估提供了有效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Adaptive assessment systems personalize learning by estimating learner proficiency and recommending suitable questions. However, many existing approaches rely on fixed difficulty labels, static rating updates, or black-box prediction models that provide limited control over rating stability, interpretability, and time-constrained routing. This paper proposes MARS, a Momentum-Aware Adaptive Rating System for interpretable adaptive assessment. MARS represents the question bank as a directed weighted knowledge graph and updates learner proficiency using dynamic rating sensitivity, response quality, and momentum-aware learner velocity. We also formulate a time-budgeted mark-maximization objective in which the policy selects questions within a fixed test duration under negative marking. Experiments on ASSISTments 2009 and MARS-SimExam evaluate MARS for prediction, rating stability, and adaptive routing. Results show that MARS provides smoother rating updates than Fixed Elo and achieves the highest score under time-budgeted negative-marking routing, improving the total score by 8.09 over the strongest baseline and reducing overtime violations from 50% to 5.6%. These results suggest that MARS is suitable for real-time, interpretable, and deployment-friendly adaptive assessment.

papers.title_en: Exploring Visual Access and Proactive AI Tutoring for Handwritten Mathematics
papers.authors: Nachiket Kotalwar, Conrad Borchers, Shubham Gandhi, Partha Sarathi Purkayastha, David Yaron, Carolyn P. Rosé
papers.evidence: 支持手写数学学习的多模态AI辅导平台
papers.tldr: 手写作答能暴露学习者的数学推理过程，但纯文本或语音对话的AI导师看不到纸面演算。作者搭建多模态辅导平台，用手机摄像头实时拍摄纸面，并让117名成人随机接受文本响应、视觉响应、视觉主动三种辅导以解微积分题。分析2,140条导师消息发现，视觉接入使辅导转向检查在写过程，主动性则提升错误识别与指令性提示。研究还开源平台、提示词、量表及255,984张带时间戳手写图像，为保留手写优势的自适应多模态辅导提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Handwritten work captures mathematical reasoning that learners may not express in typed or voice-dictated messages. We built a multimodal AI tutoring platform in which a phone camera gives the tutor a live view of learners' work on paper. In a randomized online study, 117 adults solved calculus problems with Text-Reactive, Visual-Reactive, or Visual-Proactive assistance. Analysis of 2,140 tutor messages showed that visual access shifted assistance toward checking ongoing work, while proactivity enhanced error identification and directive hints. Learners valued feedback grounded in their writing; those who received proactive help rated it as supportive, and about a third wanted it more often. These findings inform when tutors should intervene and what they should address. We release the platform, prompts, and instruments, together with 255,984 timestamped images of handwritten work linked to tutoring conversations, intervention decisions, and learning outcomes, to support multimodal tutoring systems that preserve the affordances of handwritten work while providing adaptive feedback.

papers.title_en: Bias and Reliability in Learning-Style Inference from Student--AI Dialogues: An Evaluation of GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash
papers.authors: Samaneh Zamanifard, Sajad Goudarzi, Andrew Robb
papers.evidence: 从学生-AI对话推断学习风格以支持个性化教学
papers.tldr: LLM教育个性化常需从对话推断学习风格，但推断是否可靠尚缺评估。研究以153名本科生问卷ILS标签为基准，检验GPT-4o与Gemini 2.0 Flash从短任务对话推断Felder-Silverman三维度，并比较零样本与少样本五折交叉验证。结果显示部分维度准确率中等却受多数类预测驱动，Intuitive与Global学习者被明显漏识别，少样本效果混杂甚至放大偏置，Active-Reflective不稳定。研究强调LLM生成的学习风格标签应视为不确定、易偏置信号，而非稳定学习者画像，并呼吁偏置感知评估与不确定性敏感设计。
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into educational technologies for personalized support, creating opportunities for real-time learner modeling from dialogue. This study evaluates whether GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash can infer three Felder-Silverman Learning Style Model dimensions (Active-Reflective, Sensing-Intuitive, and Sequential-Global) from short, task-focused student-AI problem-solving dialogues. Using questionnaire-derived Index of Learning Styles labels from 153 undergraduate participants, we compared deterministic zero-shot and few-shot prompting under five-fold cross-validation. Although accuracy and support-weighted F1 were moderate for Sensing-Intuitive and Sequential-Global, majority-class baselines, macro-F1, balanced accuracy, and per-class recall showed that performance was often driven by dominant-label prediction rather than reliable recognition of both classes. The models substantially under-identified Intuitive and Global learners; few-shot prompting produced mixed effects and sometimes amplified majority-class bias. Active-Reflective classification remained unstable across models. These findings indicate that LLM-generated learner-style labels should be treated as uncertain, bias-prone signals rather than stable learner profiles, and that dialogue-based personalization systems require bias-aware evaluation and uncertainty-sensitive design.

papers.title_en: "Do You Trust It... or Check It?": Exploring Children's Verification Behaviors in Game-Based Human-AI Collaboration
papers.authors: Shuning Liu, Yuxin Song, Hanbing Li, Ziyue Wang, Mingying Lan, Fei Lv
papers.evidence: 儿童在游戏化学习中核查AI建议
papers.tldr: 儿童易把流畅的AI建议当作可靠，却未必能核验其准确性与误导性。研究将AI建议嵌入生物知识推理游戏，比较伙伴型、工具型与双态Agent，并观察接受、查证、质疑、修正和继续使用等验证行为。对8–10岁儿童的初步评估结合日志、评分与访谈，发现伙伴型更促发直接质疑，工具型更引导证据寻求。儿童总体认为AI有用但会出错，质疑深度不一；研究为支持儿童批判性与证据化使用AI提供设计启示。
papers.abstract_en: Children are increasingly interacting with AI agents in learning and problem-solving contexts, where AI suggestions may appear fluent, helpful, and socially engaging. However, children may not always be able to judge whether such suggestions are accurate, incomplete, or misleading. This paper presents a game-based human-AI collaboration probe designed to examine how children verify AI suggestions during task-based interaction. The system embeds AI suggestions within a biological knowledge reasoning game and compares three Agent interaction styles: partner-like, tool-like, and dual-state Agent. Instead of treating trust as a static post-task attitude, this study focuses on children's situated verification behaviors, including acceptance, evidence checking, questioning, revision, and continued AI use. A preliminary evaluation with children aged 8-10 combined interaction logs, post-task ratings, and semi-structured interviews. The findings suggest that Agent style shaped children's engagement and response pathways: partner-like interaction tended to support direct questioning, while tool-like interaction was more associated with evidence seeking. Children generally viewed AI as useful but fallible, and their questioning behaviors varied in reasoning depth. The study contributes design insights for supporting children's critical, reflective, and evidence-based use of AI in collaborative tasks.

papers.title_en: SLA-LENS: From Classroom Transcripts to CSLA-Informed and Evidence-Linked L2 Interaction Analytics
papers.authors: Nemika Tyagi, Olga Kellert, Phanos Kareen, Nelvin Licona-Guevara
papers.evidence: LLM辅助的课堂互动转录学习分析框架
papers.tldr: 课堂二语互动中，学习者出错后的教师反馈与 uptake 如何影响下一轮，仍难以大规模、情境化标注。SLA-LENS 以互动主义 SLA 理论为框架，用 LLM 辅助把课堂转写稿映射为结构化教学标注，并生成证据可追溯的描述性分析。研究在 40 份真实在线 L2 西班牙语课堂、逾 2.1 万句级实例上，评估闭源与开源模型及 QLoRA 适配。其确定性报告层可复现参与、反馈、错误、uptake 与时间模式可视化，服务课堂话语研究、教学反思与课程设计。
papers.abstract_en: What happens after a learner makes an error, and how does the instructor's response shape the next turn? Investigating these exchanges across classrooms requires context-sensitive annotation that is difficult to scale manually. We introduce SLA-LENS, an end-to-end LLM-assisted framework that connects classroom transcripts to structured pedagogical annotations and evidence-linked descriptive analytics. Grounded in interactionist Second Language Acquisition (SLA) theory, its annotation schema captures second language learner errors, pedagogical functions, and uptake or repair while accounting for speaker roles, conversational context, and hierarchical labels. We apply the framework to 40 authentic online L2 Spanish classroom transcripts comprising over 21,000 sentence-level instances. We evaluate proprietary and open-weight LLMs, including task-specific QLoRA adaptation, using expert-reviewed gold annotations, held-out silver data, and metrics sensitive to different types of annotation error. A deterministic reporting layer generates reproducible visualizations of participation, feedback, learner errors, uptake, and temporal interaction patterns, linked to supporting transcript evidence. By making these patterns accessible and inspectable, SLA-LENS supports systematic classroom discourse research, pedagogical reflection, and curriculum design.

papers.title_en: Voice-Based AI Feedback in Higher Education: A Field Study on Quality and Actionability
papers.authors: Thilo Tamme, Leander Schilling, Anton Hantel
papers.evidence: 语音对话式AI代理在高等教育中收集学生反馈
papers.tldr: 传统期末书面评教存在回复率低、答案浅、可操作性弱等问题。该研究提出用语音对话式AI代理开展结构化访谈，基于调查模式效应、CASA与动态能力理论提出细化、社会临场与披露、可操作性三组假设。已完成慕尼黑工业大学电话AI访谈技术试点，验证可行性；主田野研究计划在MIT Sloan约60名学生课程中采用混合方法。研究将刻画语音AI作为独立反馈模态，并连接微观反馈质量与院校感知能力。
papers.abstract_en: Student feedback is a critical input for continuous improvement in higher education, yet traditional end-of-semester written surveys suffer from low response rates, superficial answers, satisficing, and limited actionability. Voice-based conversational AI agents can conduct structured interviews at scale, asking open-ended questions and probing follow-ups, and may capture richer qualitative feedback than written instruments. This research proposal asks what characteristics, depth, and strategic value feedback collected through voice-based conversational AI agents has in higher education, and whether such agents elicit detailed, honest, and actionable feedback that can support instructional improvement and institutional learning. Drawing on survey-mode-effects research, the Computers As Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, and dynamic capabilities theory, we develop three hypotheses on elaboration, social presence and disclosure, and actionability. A completed technical pilot at the Technical University of Munich established the feasibility of telephone-based AI interviews; the main field study is planned for the "Advanced Leadership Communication" course at MIT Sloan with approximately 60 students, using a convergent mixed-methods design and a four-dimensional coding framework for actionability (specificity, thematic richness, constructive orientation, contextual depth). The study extends CASA theory to evaluative educational settings, characterizes voice-based AI as a distinct feedback modality, and links micro-level feedback quality to institutional sensing capabilities.

papers.title_en: ValiAssist: Scaling LLM-generated Programming Feedback Validation by Demonstration
papers.authors: Xiaohang Tang, Rehema Abulikemu, Peng Gao, Yan Chen
papers.evidence: 生成式AI教学反馈与教师教学目标对齐
papers.tldr: 生成式AI能大规模产出编程反馈，但验证其是否符合教师教学意图十分困难，且标准往往难以预先完整表述。ValiAssist 采用“示范式验证”，从教师对AI反馈的修改中推断可复用的验证逻辑，并支持教师检查与改进该逻辑。16名教师的对比研究中，反馈与教学意图一致率从57%升至91%，纠正问题标准的准确率从32%升至77%。这表明示范式验证能把个案判断转化为显式可复用规则。
papers.abstract_en: Generative AI can create programming feedback at scale, but validating its alignment with instructors' pedagogical goals and strategies remains challenging. Instructors may struggle to fully specify validation criteria upfront, as these often emerge through inspecting concrete examples and revising misaligned feedback. We present ValiAssist, a validation-by-demonstration system that infers reusable validation logic from instructors' revisions of AI-generated feedback and allows instructors to inspect and refine that logic as it is applied across other student submissions. In a comparative study with 16 instructors, ValiAssist helped instructors create and refine validation criteria, producing feedback that better aligned with their pedagogical intent (91% vs. 57%) and more than doubling the accuracy of correcting problematic criteria (77% vs. 32%). Our findings suggest that validation by demonstration can help instructors turn judgments they know how to make on individual cases into explicit, reusable logic, while progressively clarifying where those judgments do and do not generalize.

papers.title_en: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
papers.authors: Emory Salaun, Syed Ayon, Kaleel Mahmood, Shaun Wallace
papers.evidence: 面向教育评估的抗AI教育内容生成
papers.tldr: 针对图像转文本与LLM使作业易被转录和求解的问题，AIRRI提出可读但抗机器的教育内容生成框架，结合字符/词/行距、透明度、条纹与噪声等图像变换及RayS、SurFree、ADBA对抗攻击。对Tesseract、EasyOCR与GOT-OCR2的评测显示字符和词错误率大幅上升，ADBA降效最强。该工作提供数据集与初评，能削弱图像转文本再交给LLM的自动化流程。
papers.abstract_en: The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.

papers.title_en: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
papers.authors: Xinping Wang, Jie Ma, Rui Xing, Wensong Guo, Xiayi Zhang, Jianhao Deng, Zihao Zhou, Boqian Yang, Feijuan He
papers.evidence: 面向教育应用的多模态多智能体数学推理评测基准
papers.tldr: 现有数学推理评测多聚焦纯文本最终答案，难以衡量多智能体系统的多模态能力、中间步骤可靠性与抗扰动性。作者提出MAMath-Bench，含1003题、11类、多难度与文本图像音频模态，并用细粒度里程碑标注从正确性、过程可靠性和对抗推理链扰动鲁棒性三方面评测。结果显示多智能体协作未必提升最终答案准确率，却能提高中间推理覆盖但增加冗余，且系统仍易受细微结构扰动影响。该基准为多智能体多模态数学推理提供过程感知的稳健评估。
papers.abstract_en: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. Multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown growing potential in this domain by leveraging collaboration and verification among multiple LLM agents. However, existing evaluations primarily focus on the correctness of final answers in text-only settings, offering limited insight into multimodal reasoning capabilities, the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, and robustness against reasoning errors. To address these limitations, we introduce MAMath-Bench, a process-aware benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities of MASs. MAMath-Bench comprises 1,003 problems spanning 11 mathematical categories, multiple difficulty levels, and several modalities, including text, images, and audio. It features fine-grained milestone annotations to evaluate systems across three dimensions: problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial reasoning-chain perturbations. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, multi-agent collaboration does not consistently improve final-answer accuracy over strong single LLMs. Second, collaboration can substantially enhance the coverage of intermediate reasoning, but such gains may come at the cost of increased reasoning redundancy. Third, current systems remain vulnerable to adversarial reasoning errors, particularly those involving subtle structural perturbations. The dataset is available at https://github.com/mira-ai-lab/AgentMath.
